**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**
- `script_machine` (crates/post/src/bin/post.rs:86-99) hands the engine `post::machine::mirror(parsed)` for a vendor tree and the raw file otherwise. `mirror` is the same function the app uses in `posting_mounts::machine_value_for` (crates/app/src/posting_mounts.rs:64), so the CLI and the app give the script the same machine value for every shipped `.mch`.
- No refusal is lost. The parse errors and `inverted_post_refusal` still run first on the parsed file (post.rs:132-136). The app calls the same `inverted_post_refusal` (posting_mounts.rs:139). The mirror carries `invertedAxes`, so the invert pass behaves as before.
- Static-grammar files still post as written. Always mirroring would empty them, as the decision file notes.
- No `unwrap`/`expect` was added outside tests. No new dependency, `build.rs`, script or `.github` change. The decision file is `docs/decisions/996-cli-post-mirrored-machine.md`. The PR touches no snapshots, no `CHANGELOG.md` and no process files.

**Local results** (merged with upstream/main e0cb004, post crate only)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `vendor_mch_cli` | 2 passed |
| `axis_direction_cli` | 3 passed |
| `post_engine` | 33 passed |
| `comp` | 9 passed |
| `comp_plane` | 3 passed |
| `mch_head_search` | 2 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

The `gate quick` plan (dry run) maps to the post lib and the two new `vendor_mch_cli` tests, which I ran.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- The CLI keeps the word-only `.mch` reader. The app's reader also judges the default holder against the holder library, so a holder-library refusal the app can give is not given by the CLI. This is disclosed in the PR. The CLI never gave it before, and it only refuses; it changes no posted word.
- The new tests cover only `tilthead.mch` and `vmc.mch`, both on the Fanuc post. A loop over all of `assets/machines/*.mch` asserting CLI output equals `engine::run(cps, mirror(parse_mch(..)))` would pin parity for every shipped machine. This could follow with #1002.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: f3e690c166098697217d6c82303433d90b937bbe -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Thank you for this one. The bug was real, and the fix is small and well placed.

### What looks good
- **One code path with the app.** `script_machine` (`crates/post/src/bin/post.rs:93`) calls `post::machine::mirror`. That is the same function the app's `posting_mounts::machine_value_for` (`crates/app/src/posting_mounts.rs:66`) calls, and the app's `machine` module re-exports `camcraft_post::machine::*`. There is no second derivation of what the script sees, so the two cannot drift apart.
- **Static-grammar files post unchanged.** A file without `kinematics.default.parts` still goes to the engine as raw JSON, exactly as before.
- **Refusals keep their order.** The `parse_mch` error, `inverted_post_refusal` and the `from_json` error all still run before any posting. A malformed or unknown file refuses with its name. It never falls back to "no machine". The three `axis_direction_cli` tests still pass: inverted X is mirrored, inverted Z is refused, and an unverified script is refused.
- **Default holder.** `mirror` never reads `default_holder`, so the unknown-holder name that the post's own `parse_mch` keeps (since #880) cannot reach the script or change a posted word.
- **Tests compare to the app's output.** Both new tests check that the CLI program is byte-equal to `engine::run(cps, mirror(parse_mch(file)), stream)`, which is the app's value. They also check the visible effects: G43.4 with A/B words and M8 on tilthead, and the spindle-max warning and M7 on vmc.
- **Housekeeping.** No new crate edge (`crates/post/Cargo.toml` is unchanged). No unwrap/expect outside tests. The new suite has its provenance and gate-map header. The decision file is present, and the PR body is complete (`Changelog:`, `Fixes #996`, conventional subject).

### Local results (trial-merged with current main, Windows, `core.autocrlf=true`)
The merge was clean, with no conflicts.

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: lib unit | 16 passed |
| axis_direction_cli | 3 passed |
| comp | 9 passed |
| comp_plane | 3 passed |
| mch_head_search | 2 passed |
| post_engine | 33 passed |
| vendor_mch_cli (new) | 2 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (non-blocking)
1. The tree check looks for `/kinematics/default/parts` only. A file that has a `kinematics.default` tree but no `parts` key is posted raw. `parse_mch` is probably the better judge of that case. It is harmless today, because no shipped file has that shape.
2. The test's "app program" comes from the post crate's `parse_mch`, not the app's holder-judging `parse_mch`. The PR body already says so, and that judgment only refuses, so the posted words are the same.
3. As the PR body says, the follow-up for the #926 recorded runner (`crates/post/tests/recorded/mod.rs`) is to pass the file straight through once #1002 merges.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
